text:
rohit: FYI customer AcmePayments opened a support ticket — Dedicated pool 'acme-ded-3' p95 spiked to ~2.2s and we started seeing 429s at 02:00 UTC, throughput down ~45% since then
sophie: any autoscale events around that time?
infra-bot: autoscaler: scaleDown triggered for acme-ded-3 at 01:58:47 UTC (reason: target-util < 0.5)
rohit: interesting — scaleDown right before spike. Could be flapping + scheduler interaction
frank: getting their metrics now, attaching quick distro: queue_depth jumped to 380, avg_batch_tokens went from ~800 to ~3400 at 02:01 UTC
elaine: that's the clue — max_batch_tokens for that pool is 4096 due to a profile change last week; lots of small requests + continuous batcher created huge microbatches
sophie: can you paste the batcher debug log?
frank: snippet from batcher stdout around 02:00:
```
[I] 02:00:57 batching_window closed: 120ms, collected 310 reqs, total_tokens=345600
[I] 02:00:57 schedule -> microbatch[0]: tokens=345600, est_runtime=2100ms
[E] 02:02:00 request_timeout: microbatch exceeded per-batch timeout
```
rohit: est_runtime 2100ms matches p95. So one huge microbatch blocked the GPU and starved other queues, causing 429 downstream
elaine: also saw scheduler quantum stuck: the low-priority tenant prefill was forcing prefix caching to favor re-use which delayed microbatch flushes
sophie: reproduce steps? we need minimal repro to test a fix on staging
rohit: script we used locally:
```
# flood with many short requests
for i in $(seq 1 400); do 
  curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT -d '{"input":"hi"}' &
done
```
frank: repro on staging when max_batch_tokens >= 4000 and continuous_batching=true -> queue depth grows and single batch accumulates
elaine: immediate mitigation: reduce max_batch_tokens to 2048 for that pool and set continuous_batching.max_window_ms=50
sophie: also propose scheduler change: increase microbatch concurrency (concurrent_microbatches=4) so large batches are split earlier rather than one giant schedule
ops-bot: created incident ENG-5689, assigned to eng-runtime oncall
rohit: customer-facing: tell AcmePayments we've identified batching-size regression tied to a recent profile change, temporarily throttling their higher-concurrency job and applying a pool config rollback; ETA 30m
frank: making the config change now: running redwoodctl apply-config --pool acme-ded-3 --set 'max_batch_tokens=2048,continuous_batching.max_window_ms=50'
infra-bot: config apply succeeded on node-12,node-13 at 02:12:04 UTC
elaine: after change tail of metrics: queue_depth down to ~40 in 4m, p95 down to 180ms
sophie: schedule followups: (1) add a guard to reject batches where total_tokens > 250k (2) backfill test that simulates large numbers of tiny requests with prefix caching on (3) revert profile change in next canary
rohit: I'll draft the customer message and coordinate with CS; frank/elaine please run a canary patch with scheduler split heuristics this afternoon
frank: ack, will run canary at 16:00 UTC and link results here
elaine: also adding an alert rule: alert if avg_batch_tokens > 3000 for >60s
sophie: thanks team. keep updates concise in this thread and paste any postmortem link once available
rohit: noted, updating ticket and pinging CS now :phone:
